explanations: C-1. Compared with no Tamberlay Home Start Grant, compliance cost for buyers.first_time rises from the short run onward (tier A, invisible). Why: CR-8: every payment is a receipt: what one side no longer pays or receives is what the other keeps or loses. This holds if: no assumption. Reported.

C-2. Compared with no Tamberlay Home Start Grant, job changes for buyers.first_time falls from the short run onward (tier B, invisible). Why: RS-11: a benefit lost on moving ties the holder to staying put. This holds if: Some recipients would otherwise move within the repayment period (p = 0.70); Many eligible recipients value the payment above the cost of qualifying, and claim it (p = 0.90). Reported.

C-3. Compared with no Tamberlay Home Start Grant, price paid for buyers.first_time falls from the short run onward (tier B, visible). Why: SB-2: a payment per unit is a wedge in the other direction: buyers pay less net of it, sellers may receive more, and more is traded. This holds if: Sellers do not capture the whole payment: the recipients' net price falls (p = 0.70); Many eligible recipients value the payment above the cost of qualifying, and claim it (p = 0.90). Reported.

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-020; judged from the text: a $15,000 grant against the cost of qualifying (24 months in the home, declarations) for a pool of about 18,000 first-time buyers a year, with 20,000 grants funded.

question.text: Will many of those eligible claim the payment, because it is worth more to them than what they must do or give up to qualify?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-1: prices under the cap rise by less than the grant, because many buyers in the segment get no grant and some supply responds.

question.text: Will the recipients keep part of the payment, rather than sellers raising their prices by the whole of it?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-4: some renters at the margin buy sooner because of the grant (the deposit binds first-time buyers).

question.text: Will more of the subsidized good change hands than without the payment (because buyers buy more, or sellers can supply more)?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-2: the supply of homes under the cap responds slowly (approval 12 to 24 months, construction 9 to 15).

question.text: Is the sellers' supply of the subsidized good fixed for a while (stock ordered or built before the payment, long lead times), so that it cannot grow at once to meet the added demand?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-20: while supply is slow, owners of homes under the cap have clearly fewer alternatives than first-time buyers, who can keep renting, wait, buy above the cap or buy in Lowen.

question.text: While their supply is fixed, do the sellers have clearly fewer alternatives than the recipients (who can wait, buy something else or not buy at all)?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-2: the supply of homes under the cap responds slowly.

question.text: Is the supply of the asset whose return the payment raises (land, homes, licenses, specific plant) fixed or slow to expand?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-3: buyers, sellers and builders expect the grant to last at least through Year 4.

question.text: Do buyers of the affected assets expect the payment to stay in place long enough to raise what the assets earn over several years?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-7: couples can arrange title or partner declarations so that a prior owner's household qualifies (declaration-based partner check, no register outside Tamberlay).

question.text: For some who do not now meet the criteria, will changing what they do or own so as to meet them cost less than the payment is worth to them?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-17: owners, builders and agents can organize to lobby at a cost below their stake.

question.text: Can the sellers who gain from the payment organize to lobby for its extension or renewal at a cost below their stake (an existing trade association, a few large firms)?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-5: first-time buyers knew of the grant from March and could delay.

question.text: Could those who will be eligible put off a purchase they would otherwise make before the payment starts, until it does (the payment was announced in advance)?

answer.rationale: No matching assumption in WE-020; judged from the text: first-time buyers in a three-year window are mostly households that would buy within a few years anyway; the text gives no sign that the window creates buyers who never would.

question.text: Would many of those who buy during the payment's window have bought the same good within the following few years anyway?

answer.rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-9: some recipients receive job offers in the first 24 months that would require moving.

question.text: Would some recipients, without the repayment condition, take a job or a home elsewhere within the period in which moving means repaying the payment?

source_sentences: The grant is $15,000 for first-time buyers who apply, paid at settlement and usable toward the deposit, for the purchase of a home in Tamberlay.
The contract price must be $450,000 or less (fixed in money terms).
The home must be the buyer's principal residence for 24 months; otherwise the full grant is repaid.
Neither the applicant nor the applicant's spouse or declared partner has ever owned residential property, anywhere.
The governor announced the grant in the budget speech on 10 March of Year 1.
It applies to purchase contracts signed from 1 July of Year 1 to 30 June of Year 4, with a legislative review in Year 3.
Renewal is possible but not promised.
The grant and its administration are funded by an annual appropriation from general revenue, about $300 million a year (20,000 grants).
The State Revenue Office checks the land register and declarations, and checks occupancy against driver's license and electoral roll addresses.

context: About 60,000 homes are sold there in a normal year, roughly a third of them for $450,000 or less, and first-time buyers account for about 18,000 purchases.
Builders complete about 12,000 new homes a year; zoning approval and permits take 12 to 24 months and construction another 9 to 15, so the stock of homes responds slowly to prices.
Tamberlay's largest city, Kessford, sits on the border with the state of Lowen, whose suburbs are within a 30-minute commute and which has no comparable grant.
Entry-level home prices in Tamberlay have been rising about 4% a year.
